clarification: Run 2: existing fixnum 01, nil 3, t 7 and legacy 000 boxes keep decoding unchanged. Every possible new-tag recipient moves behind S1 before S2. This clarifies the criterion, not its threshold.
alignment_argument: Four even classes fit 8-byte alignment while preserving the low-bit immediate test. Sixteen-byte alignment offers eight even classes but adds padding and does not repair old decoders. Keep 8 until measured type pressure justifies 16.
coexistence: Only 000 enters legacy Sexp offsets. Accessors dispatch all even classes, normalize type-specific identity, and trace both parent/child layouts. New pointer classes never pass through a raw even-means-box branch.
refcount: A live lock-xadd reader/writer remains in nelisp_nlconsbox_clone, but its result is discarded; no active drop or GC reader uses the count. Remove the RMW and all initializers, retire/guard old drop/layout consumers, prove linked reader/writer count zero on every platform, then shrink 24-byte payload to16. Do not truncate first.

immediates.legacy: Low-bit tests, arithmetic shift by2, and literals3/7 are unchanged. Integer helpers retain their integer-only precondition. For every signed 62-bit n, signed64((n*4+1))>>2=n, including both extrema.
immediates.new_tag: Parity-only predicates remain valid; integer-only helpers must not receive pointer WORDs.

tags.legacy: Immediate discrimination and tag loads at legacy address+0 retain their inputs and memory layout; native dyn/static probes exercise nil/t/fixnums/legacy integer/cons.
tags.new_tag: S1 must centralize semantic-tag dispatch; direct reads allowed only for explicit 000 views.

payload.legacy: Existing immediate integer shifts and legacy payload@8 are unchanged. wf_bytecode_w_int receives integers only; no cons is valid under that precondition.
payload.new_tag: Generic payload extraction moves behind S1; integer-only branches retain strict numeric preconditions.

inline_tg2.legacy: Comparing semantic tag2 retains its meaning for immediate or boxed integers; existing tag providers see unchanged legacy encodings.
inline_tg2.new_tag: All eight enclosing functions must obtain tg from the S1 semantic accessor before new tags reach them.

containers.legacy: 000 addresses the same header/payload and 8-byte WORD slots. Native probes preserve cons car=t/cdr=nil; errors and identity retain existing caller contracts.
containers.new_tag: S1 must mask/dispatch types and preserve mixed parent/child identity and error data before S2.

views.legacy: Existing even WORDs still address full32-byte views; immediate adapters keep the same encoding and root lifetime.
views.new_tag: S1 must remove the even=>32-byte-copy assumption. A direct16-byte cons must never feed a 32-byte copy.

identity.legacy: 000 box/payload addresses and immediate equality inputs are unchanged; hashing and positioned-symbol storage keep their legacy interpretation.
identity.new_tag: S1 defines type-specific canonical identity, mixed legacy/direct eq, cycle handling and compatible hashes.

gc.legacy: Unchanged slots/marking recognize the same odd immediates and exact legacy block addresses; pool WORD marker215 remains separate from Sexp tags.
gc.new_tag: S1 masks before block lookup and traces by representation, with forced GC and cross-thread roots for every mixed layout.

image_walk.legacy: Legacy slot offsets, exact block starts and raw intern-table pointers remain unchanged.
image_walk.new_tag: S1 must enumerate new child fields, mask block addresses and retain pointer tag bits in relocation entries.

relocation.legacy: 000 offsets have zero tag bits; adding an aligned arena base preserves current relocation behavior. Image header roots are also restored as offsets.
relocation.new_tag: S1 requires (base+untag(offset))|tag, untagged bounds checks, raw intern addresses unchanged, and S7 format bump/stale rejection.

codegen.legacy: The generated instruction stream sees the same WORD encoding and explicit view layout; S0 changes no runtime source or executable.
codegen.new_tag: S1 accessor ABI must cover emitted raw tag/payload loads and reader/printer/error data boundaries; source grep alone is not a complete inventory.

ffi.legacy: External pointers remain raw C addresses/integers; existing Lisp WORD marshalling sees unchanged encoding.
ffi.new_tag: Only Lisp WORD arguments use new accessors; pin actual objects, not transient views. Keep C pointers untagged.

foreign_scalar.legacy: The foreign scalar0 (word&3)==2 contract is distinct from NeLisp fixnum01; keep its explicit nl_imm_int conversion and authentication boundary.
foreign_scalar.new_tag: Do not reinterpret this foreign tag as a new Lisp pointer class; S1 must audit conversion callers.

gc.count_rule: nl_gc_stats+24 increments in debt_rearm once after each nonrecursive outer nl_gc_sweep_merge_chunks, not per recursively visited chunk
differing_inputs: last-sweep live bytes including permanent generation
initial hole map and reserved-growth watermark
gc.cause_limit: GC code is identical. Image free/nonfree maps differ. Conservative bake retention and transient roots can cause this; the specific historical retention event cannot be reconstructed from saved images.
gc.reset_boundary: After precise-root bake quiescence, release transient compiler/source roots, collect twice and hash the live/hole census before freezing. For comparisons reset an explicit requested-allocation debt budget at the same workload semantic boundary, arm it immediately, and report emergency growth collections separately. A fixed floor alone does not reset the two initial unarmed sweeps or growth watermark.

S1.new: same zero target; census all WORD/view, GC/image/FFI/codegen boundaries with a failing mutation and instruction-provenance limits
S1.reason: Every new-tag recipient must be covered before layout flips.

S2.old: cons arena bytes<=24 with rc / <=16 without rc
S2.new: cons arena bytes<=32 with rc / <=24 without rc; payload<=24 / <=16; make-list and individually retained populations both pass; linked count readers/writers=0 before shrink
S2.reason: Arena field4 includes an 8-byte allocator prefix. Current ABI alias overhead is separately visible; deleting a header cannot eliminate allocator metadata.

S3.new: string8<=48 arena bytes; symbol handle<=32 with shared name storage charged separately; name identity/eq and mutation parity
S3.reason: Single tagged handle plus aligned payload and allocator prefix; sharing must not hide an uncharged name allocation.

S4.new: same zero-header target; vector slot8; one-user-slot record<=32 arena bytes; char-table/closure/frame tracing and mixed identity; implement S4 before S2
S4.reason: Cold/Anvil cons below60%; container/frame and alias ownership must be made explicit before cons-only savings predictions.

S5.old: all remaining types carry no32-byte header box
S5.new: same zero-header target; float<=24, measured one-limb bignum<=32, detached two-field marker<=40 arena bytes; GNU numeric/error parity
S5.reason: Payload plus allocator prefix; current float40, bignum64 and marker272 constructor slopes require distinct limits.

S6.new: legacy headers/views/root allocations=0; materialisers/copies=0; roots8; separately classify legitimate32-byte payloads
S6.reason: The literal size is shared by real payloads and legacy views. A typed census retains zero representation debt without banning legitimate data.

S7.old: format bump/stale rejection, Windows acceptance, library images rebuilt
S7.new: unchanged; both loader/relocator paths mask pointer tags before bounds checks; native Windows and independently rebuilt library evidence required
S7.reason: Aligned base addition preserves000 only; new tags require explicit relocation semantics.

S8.old: provisional live vendor-load<=50% of baseline; files/regex/boot total-Ir caps;400-call soak
S8.new: retain provisional<=50%, pinned ABI executable+image baseline and fixed vendor-load recipe frozen before S1; unchanged total-Ir caps over4 layouts including GC and400-call soak
S8.reason: These snapshots are not the fixed vendor-load experiment. No measured evidence supports changing50% yet; differing frozen generations invalidate date-only baseline identities.

stage_order_reason: Cons is below60% in the primary Anvil and cold heaps even under an exhaustive layout upper bound. Move container/frame work S4 before S2; retain S6 after object conversions because its zero-header end state cannot precede them. Library's physical-cons share is reported independently and does not justify a cons-only forecast for the other heaps.
